name: Chale Wote Street Art Festival
funding: Free street festival (15th edition Aug 2025) by ACCRA [dot] ALT; 2023 supported by Ghana's tourism ministry, Ghana Tourism Authority, Citi FM, Institut Français.

name: Gallery 1957
funding: Commercial gallery founded in 2016 by British Lebanese construction owner Marwan Zakhem. Its Yaa Asantewaa Art Prize pays GHC 50,000 to the winner.

name: Nubuke Foundation
funding: Private foundation from 2006. Funded through the EU and OACPS ACP-EU Culture programme (AWA consortium with Institut français) and the British Council Digital Collaboration Fund.

name: blaxTARLINES KUMASI
funding: Art network and incubator tied to the KNUST painting and sculpture department in Kumasi.

name: Savannah Centre for Contemporary Art (SCCA Tamale)
Onassis Stegi
funding: Run by the Alexander S. Onassis Foundation, funded entirely by profits of its Business Foundation, which invests in shipping and real estate. Corporate sponsors exist; no budget is published.

name: MOMus
funding: State museum group under the Greek Ministry of Culture.

name: Museo Ixchel del Traje Indígena
funding: Small private textile museum on the UFM campus; paid for by membership tiers (Q300 to Q10,000), the US charity Friends of the Ixchel Museum (since 1984) and project grants.

name: Museo Nacional de Arte Moderno Carlos Mérida (MUNAM)
funding: State museum of the Ministerio de Cultura y Deportes, which spent over Q16M (about US$2M) on roof and museography works in 2023-25.

name: Musée National de Guinée (Sandervalia)
funding: State museum being rebuilt with a €16M concessional AFD (France) loan signed 30 Mar 2026; the Guinean state funds operations.

name: Kling & Bang
funding: Thyssen-Bornemisza Art Contemporary supports its annual curatorial program.
